description: Returns the set of appids already persisted for a given run and source, so acquisition can skip re-fetching them when a stage is re-attempted after a crash or a cooperative cancellation (ADR-014). This is what makes stage-granular resume cheap: acquisition calls this before each batch and only requests appids missing from the returned set.
signature: def read_fetched_appids(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, source: str) -> set[int]
docstring:
List appids already fetched and persisted for one run and source.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run to check.
    source: One of 'steamspy_all', 'steamspy_appdetails', 'steam_appdetails', 'steam_reviews'.

Returns:
    A set of appids present in raw_games for that (run_id, source) pair. Empty set if none.
postconditions: The returned set is exactly the distinct appid values of raw_games rows matching (run_id, source) -- no more, no fewer

Calling upsert_raw_payloads for a subset of the returned set is a correct no-op (INSERT OR IGNORE), so a caller does not need read_fetched_appids to be perfectly race-free against a concurrent writer on the same connection's thread

edge_cases.input: run_id has no raw_games rows for the given source at all (stage never attempted, or a different source)
source is not one of the four allowed values
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError before querying, consistent with other CHECK-backed parameters across storage

edge_cases.input: A very large run (tens of thousands of appids)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns a single set built from one query; acceptable because appid is a small int and the whole candidate set already fits in memory as pandas frames elsewhere in the pipeline

unit_tests.name: test_returns_persisted_appids
unit_tests.description: After upsert_raw_payloads writes payloads for appids {1,2,3} under source='steam_appdetails', read_fetched_appids returns exactly that set.

unit_tests.name: test_empty_for_unattempted_source
unit_tests.description: A run with only steamspy_all payloads returns an empty set for steam_reviews.

unit_tests.name: test_invalid_source_raises
unit_tests.description: An out-of-vocabulary source string raises StorageError.
